mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes V Class V200d or V220d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A V200d or V220d engine replacement typically costs between £2,500 and £4,300 depending on engine code (OM651.901, OM651.911 or OM651.931), condition type, and whether fitting is included. Rebuilt OM651.901 (V200d): £2,500-£4,000 supply only. Rebuilt OM651.911 (V220d, 2014-2019): £2,600-£4,300 supply only. Rebuilt OM651.931 (V220d, 2019-2024): £2,700-£4,500 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £1,400-£3,500 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What causes the OM651 timing chain rattle on cold start in a V200d or V220d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651 timing chain rattle is caused by tensioner failure allowing oil pressure loss, leading to chain stretch and guide wear. The chain is at the rear of the engine - most repairs require engine removal. Early W447 models (2014-2016) are most vulnerable to timing chain issues. Cold-start rattling indicates chain elongation requiring full engine-out replacement. Rebuilt OM651 units include updated tensioner seals and hardened guide rails as standard.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of injector seal failure on a V200d or V220d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651's injector seals typically show warning signs before complete failure. Loss of power and rough idle. Diesel pooling in the valve cover around injectors. Increased oil consumption and sludge buildup. Check engine light with rail pressure error codes. Hard starting when warm.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my V200d or V220d engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., timing chain tensioner, injector seals, EGR cooler). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic timing chain failure. OM651 timing chain replacement: £1,200-£1,800 - do this if rattle is persistent. Injector seal replacement: £250-£450 - catch it early. Full OM651 rebuild: £3,500-£4,800 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Given V Class V200d / V220d values (£12,000-£30,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my V200d or V220d has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on a machined flat on the engine block - on OM651, front of the block on the driver's side. V200d (2014-2019): OM651.901 (2.1L diesel, 136hp). V220d (2014-2019): OM651.911 (2.1L diesel, 163hp). V220d (2019-2024): OM651.931 (2.1L diesel, 163hp).

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used V200d or V220d engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a V Class diesel. The W447 engine bay layout, 7G-TRONIC gearbox alignment, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. Engine removal requires proper lifting equipment and subframe lowering. ECU coding and injector calibration require Mercedes-Benz Star Diagnosis tools. AdBlue system recalibration needed on Euro 6 models. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,500 - worth every penny.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes V Class V200d / V220d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes Benz V Class V200d and V220d form the backbone of the W447 generation V Class range, powered by the OM651 2.1-litre four-cylinder turbo-diesel. These engines deliver the perfect balance of economy and performance for airport transfers, hotel shuttles and large family transport, with the V200d offering 136hp and the V220d delivering 163hp.

milestones.description: W447 V Class launched with OM651.901 (V200d, 136hp) and OM651.911 (V220d, 163hp), 7G-TRONIC automatic transmission, Euro 6 emissions
Facelift introduces OM651.931 for late V220d models with refined emissions calibration
OM651.901 updated with improved timing chain components
OM654 2.0L diesel begins to replace OM651 in some V250d and V300d variants, but V200d and V220d retain OM651

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes V Class V200d / V220d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes V Class V200d and V220d rely on the OM651 2.1-litre diesel - a robust commercial workhorse that has developed a well-documented reputation for specific, predictable failures. Timing chain tensioner wear dominates replacement demand on early W447 models, while injector seal degradation and EGR cooler issues also drive significant repair enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common V Class V200d and V220d engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the V200d / V220d Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The OM651's timing chain is located at the rear of the engine block. A faulty tensioner allows oil pressure loss, causing chain slack and a characteristic rattle on cold start. The chain stretches and guides wear over time. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, leading to catastrophic valve and piston interference.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner and seal only - engine-in-situ
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if caught very early with no chain stretch

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine-out replacement of chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Required if rattle is persistent or chain has stretched

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with upgraded tensioner, new timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if chain has jumped or guides have failed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W447 V Class V200d or V220d is worth £12,000-£30,000 depending on age and mileage - the full replacement cost of £3,500-£4,800 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples. For vehicles worth under £10,000, evaluate repair options carefully.
problems.recommendation: If you are hearing a metallic rattle at cold start on a V Class under 90,000 miles, a preventative timing chain replacement is the most cost-effective route. However, if the chain has already jumped timing or damaged the cylinder head, a full rebuilt OM651 engine is the only financially sensible option to avoid repeated downtime and costly collateral repairs.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 engine prices for your Mercedes V200d / V220d

problems.h4: OM651 Injector Seal Failure - Why the V200d / V220d Loses Power and Idles Roughly
problems.rootCause: Degrading injector copper seals allow combustion gases into the crankcase, carbonising pistons and oil rings. Early piezo injectors can also fail (particularly on pre-2012 units), causing rough idle and rail pressure errors.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace injector copper seals, clean injector bores, oil change
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before ring damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all four injectors with updated magnetic type, code to ECU
repairOptions.longevity: Required if piezo injector failure or multiple seals failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete supply & fit, updated seals, tested fuel system, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Guaranteed resolution; eliminates hidden cylinder wall scoring

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a V Class V200d or V220d worth £12,000-£30,000, injector seal replacement at £250-£450 is a sensible repair. Full engine replacement is only justified if compression loss or bottom-end damage is present.
problems.recommendation: We recommend a full reconditioned engine if compression drops across any cylinder or if fuel dilution of the oil is detected. Partial fixes on a heavily carbon-damaged OM651 rarely survive commercial delivery cycles, making a complete rebuilt unit the most cost-effective long-term investment for fleet operators.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 Mercedes V Class V200d / V220d engine prices

problems.group: OM651 EGR Cooler & AdBlue System Failures
problems.h4: OM651 EGR Cooler & AdBlue System Failures - Why the V200d / V220d Triggers Emissions Warnings
problems.rootCause: EGR coolers accumulate carbon deposits from stop-start urban driving and develop internal micro-cracks from thermal stress. AdBlue injector crystallisation blocks the dosing system, triggering countdown warnings on Euro 6 models.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler, clean EGR valve, reset adaptions
repairOptions.longevity: Resolves power loss and warning lights

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace AdBlue injector, flush system, reset SCR counter
repairOptions.longevity: Required if crystallisation has damaged the dosing module

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM651 with new EGR components, emissions system calibrated
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary for persistent emissions failures

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a V Class V200d or V220d worth £12,000-£30,000, EGR cooler replacement at £950-£1,350 is a sensible repair. Full engine replacement is only justified if emissions system failure has caused secondary damage.
problems.recommendation: On a V Class used primarily for airport transfers or motorway cruising, EGR systems clog less frequently. However, if your vehicle operates in heavy city traffic, an EGR cooler replacement is a practical mid-term fix. If the crack has allowed coolant into the combustion chamber, a full rebuilt engine is strongly advised to prevent catastrophic cylinder scoring.
